title: SCP
description:
Spatial Context Packet. FROZEN INTERFACE #3.

Recomputed on-device at 10Hz and pushed to the model as conversation context. MUST stay under ~2KB serialised — at 10Hz a 4KB packet is 40KB/s of uplink competing with the audio stream, and the latency budget does not survive that. If a field would push it over, the field is wrong.

Why 10Hz and not once per turn: the user sweeps the phone across the room WHILE speaking, and that sweep is the pointing gesture. 'Put it over there' lands 300-600ms after the wrist stopped moving, so the referent is in a packet from the recent past, not the one at end-of-speech. `last_floor_hit` exists for exactly this.

The client scores candidates; the model only confirms. Never ask the model to do geometry.

t.description: Epoch milliseconds at which this packet was sampled.

forward.description: Unit view direction in room space.

crosshair_ray.title: CrosshairRay
crosshair_ray.description: What the centre of the screen is on RIGHT NOW.

hit_entity.description: Entity id, or null when hit_type is `none`.

pointing_ray.title: PointingRay
pointing_ray.description:
WHERE THE RAY COMES FROM. The deixis ray is not always the screen centre: when hand tracking has the user's index finger, the ray is camera -> fingertip pixel and the fingertip becomes a movable crosshair. `screen_point` is that pixel; [0.5, 0.5] is the centre and means the ray degenerates to the phone crosshair.

Only the SOURCE of the ray lives here. Every downstream consumer still reads `crosshair_ray` and `visible_entities[].angular_offset_deg`, both of which are computed FROM this ray by the client. That is why hand tracking needs no change to the scorer: it changes which ray the builder measures against, not how candidates are ranked.

`source` is `phone` whenever confidence is below the tracker's gate, so a dropped hand degrades to the existing behaviour on that frame rather than freezing on a stale fingertip.

screen_point.description: Normalised VIEWPORT coordinates, [0,0] top-left to [1,1] bottom-right. Not Vision's bottom-left image space — the provider converts. [0.5, 0.5] is the crosshair.

confidence.description: Tracker confidence in the fingertip. Always 1 when source is `phone`: the screen centre is not a guess.

source.description: Which input produced the ray on this frame. Flips per frame; the UI shows it so a failing tracker is visible rather than silent.

last_floor_hit.title: LastFloorHit
last_floor_hit.description: CRITICAL. The most recent point where the crosshair ray met the floor, with its age. 'Over there' resolves against this, not against the current frame — by the time speech ends the phone has usually moved off the spot. Keep the freshest hit within roughly the last 2s; older than that, treat as stale and ask.

age_ms.description: Milliseconds since the hit. Null point means there has been no floor hit this session.

last_tap.title: LastTap
last_tap.description: An explicit disambiguation the user made by touching the screen. Outranks every scoring heuristic while fresh.

visible_entities.description: On-screen entities, nearest-to-crosshair first. Capped at 12 to hold the 2KB budget — anything past the 12th was never going to be the referent of a demonstrative.

class.description: refined_class when known, else the RoomPlan class. This is the word the model will say out loud.

angular_offset_deg.description: Angle between the crosshair ray and the entity centre. The dominant term in the deixis score.

screen_area_frac.description: Fraction of the viewport the entity covers. Separates 'the big thing right there' from a distant thing at the same angle.

salience.description: INTRINSIC prominence, carried over from the RSG, where it is seeded by footprint area — big things are more likely referents. Distinct from `salience_stack`, which is conversational recency: a wardrobe nobody has mentioned is highly salient and not at all recent. Scorer.rank needs both and reads only this packet, so it has to be here.

salience_stack.description: Entity ids, MOST RECENT FIRST — what has been talked about or touched this session. Resolves anaphora ('now move it back') with no geometry at all.

ranked_candidates.description: The client's answer to 'what does the demonstrative mean'. The model picks from this list; it does not compute it. When the top two scores are within 0.1 the client has already decided it is ambiguous — the model must ask, not guess.

demonstrative.description: Which demonstrative this candidate is the best fit for. `this` favours near+centred, `that` far+centred, `there` the floor hit, `it` the salience stack.

free_space_summary.title: FreeSpaceSummary
free_space_summary.description: A two-number answer to 'does it fit'. Cheap enough to recompute at 10Hz, which a full occupancy grid is not — and small enough to send, which the grid also is not.

wall_clearances.description: Per-wall free depth measured outward from the wall face.
